releases.title: Your workout, live

highlights.title: Live workout clock
highlights.text: Total time ticks at the top of your workout, always in view.

highlights.title: Running totals
highlights.text: Kilos lifted, sets, reps and exercises done update as you tick sets.

highlights.title: Fun milestones
highlights.text: See what you've lifted so far: a grizzly bear, a dairy cow, a small car…

changes: The Workout header stays pinned and shows the total time, kg (or lb) lifted, sets, reps and completed exercises
A fun line compares your total to animals and vehicles, with the next milestone to beat
Totals update as you tick sets, complete exercises or edit a logged set

releases.title: Pick. Lift. Log.

highlights.title: A logo of its own
highlights.text: A dumbbell on the rise: lime plates and two teal motion lines.

highlights.title: Launch screen
highlights.text: The dumbbell draws itself and the tagline appears for about 2 seconds; tap to skip.

highlights.title: Branded everywhere
highlights.text: The logo sits in the header, on the empty Workout tab and in the README.

changes: New Go2FGym logo (dumbbell on the rise): docs/logo.svg and a 1024 px app icon, docs/icon-1024.png
Launch screen shown for 2.4 s with a short animation and the tagline "Pick. Lift. Log."; tap to skip; still with Reduce Motion (shared launch-screen blueprint 1.0.0)
Logo mark and Go2FGym wordmark in the header, the logo on the Workout tab when it is empty, and at the top of the README
Settings › Built with lists the launch-screen blueprint

releases.title: Fewer mis-taps

highlights.title: Complete in the corner
highlights.text: The round green check sits at the top of each exercise, away from the set ticks.

highlights.title: Tap to start
highlights.text: Tap an exercise or start typing in it and it's marked In progress.

highlights.title: Review finished exercises
highlights.text: Tap a completed exercise to see its sets; ↺ Resume only when you mean it.

changes: Complete moved from next to Add set to a round green check in the top-right corner of each exercise; Remove moved to the bottom row
Tapping an exercise card, or typing in its weight or reps, marks it In progress and highlights it; an exercise that was only tapped steps back when you start another
Tapping a completed exercise opens a review with every set and the start and finish time, plus Exercise page and ↺ Resume
↺ Resume reopens a completed exercise as In progress
fixes: Complete sat right below the last set's tick, so it was easy to hit by mistake
Tapping a completed exercise reopened it instead of just showing it

releases.title: Train in your own order

highlights.title: Drag to reorder
highlights.text: Hold the ⠿ handle on any exercise and drag it where you want it.

highlights.title: Up next
highlights.text: One tap moves an exercise right after the ones you've started, ideal for supersets.

highlights.title: Complete and move on
highlights.text: Complete folds an exercise into one line with kg, reps and time, and jumps to the next.

changes: Drag and drop exercises in a workout by the ⠿ handle, with touch or mouse; the list scrolls while you drag
↑ Up next moves an exercise right after the exercises in progress, or to the top of the open ones
✓ Complete marks the remaining logged sets done, folds the exercise into one line (muscle group, kg lifted, reps, minutes spent) and moves it to the completed stack at the top
The next exercise is highlighted (In progress or Up now) and scrolled into view
Tap a completed line to reopen it
Each ticked set records its time, so time spent per exercise is shown

releases.title: Easier to get around

highlights.title: Add exercises anytime
highlights.text: ＋ Add exercises in the workout header opens the list for that workout's muscles.

highlights.title: Quick preview
highlights.text: Tap the eye on any exercise in your workout to see it moving, without leaving.

highlights.title: Clear way back
highlights.text: Bigger back buttons, and a Workout button on every Train screen while you train.

changes: ＋ Add exercises in the Workout header and under the exercises opens the exercise list filtered to the workout's muscle groups, with a short hint
✓ Workout (n) button in the header of the exercise list and exercise pages while a workout is running
Built plans: Start in the header, Start and add exercises at the bottom, and ‹ Options instead of ‹ Settings
Preview pop-up from the eye button on workout and plan exercises: photo demo, muscles, last time, and Open exercise; closes itself after 10 seconds with a countdown
Back buttons are now clearly visible buttons instead of small text links
Empty Workout tab offers Choose muscles and, with an AI key, Build next workout

releases.title: No more black screen

highlights.title: Opens reliably
highlights.text: If iOS fails to start the screen on opening, the app now notices and reloads it by itself.

changes: Startup problems are noted in startup-log.txt next to the app's data, to help track down rare issues
fixes: Opening the app sometimes showed a black screen until it was closed and opened again

releases.title: A tidier header

highlights.title: Tidier header
highlights.text: The Settings button now sits neatly in the top bar at every text size.

fixes: The Settings button on the Train tab overlapped the line under the Go2FGym header
With Large or Larger text, the 7AM Club link pushed the Settings button off the screen

releases.title: Settings, your way

highlights.title: A real Settings screen
highlights.text: Equipment, kg or lb, rest timer, backup and AI coach in one place, behind the sliders icon.

highlights.title: Colours and layout
highlights.text: Six palettes or Auto, plus Compact and a one-line Tiny layout for long lists.

highlights.title: Text size and font
highlights.text: Pick Small to Larger text and the condensed or a serif headline font.

changes: New Settings sheet (sliders icon on the Train tab): Appearance, Workout, Library, History, AI coach, Updates, Timing, Downloads and Built with; changes apply at once, nothing to edit in the code
Appearance shared with the other apps: Auto plus six palettes (Go2FGym red in all), Comfortable, Compact or Tiny layout, four text sizes, condensed or serif headlines
Tiny layout: one line per exercise without photos and one line per workout in History; logging sets stays full size
Equipment and exercise types are switches; the library updates when you close Settings, and Update library fetches photos for new equipment
Rest timer and photo downloads are adjustable with ranges and Reset
Check for updates now, in Settings › Updates
Settings are saved in settings.json in iCloud Drive › Scriptable › Go2FGym, so updates no longer undo your changes
AI settings moved from the Train tab footer into Settings › AI coach
Built with: the blueprints this app follows, with links to read them

releases.title: Your AI coach, Claude or OpenAI

highlights.title: Claude or OpenAI
highlights.text: Workout plans, reviews and Strava posts now work with either provider. Switch any time in AI settings.

highlights.title: Pick any model
highlights.text: Load the models your own key can use, choose one and test the connection.

highlights.title: See your token usage
highlights.text: Tokens per day, feature and model, so you always know what AI costs you.

changes: New AI settings sheet (Train tab › AI settings): Claude and OpenAI keys, model picker loaded from your key, connection test, token usage per day, feature and model
Keys are entered in a native secure prompt and stored in the iOS Keychain; the page only ever sees them masked
Every AI coach request goes through one shared AI call, following the app-blueprints AI configuration
One switch under What AI does turns the after-workout review and Strava post on or off
Without a key, AI-only buttons are hidden and the Strava post offers the Neutral template, labelled “Template — no AI”
Workout plans, reviews and Strava posts are labelled with the provider that wrote them
Your existing OpenAI key moves over automatically
The thinking-effort setting is gone: choose a model instead

releases.title: Never miss an update

highlights.title: Update reminders
highlights.text: The app tells you when a new version is out, and waits two days if you tap Later.

highlights.title: One-tap update
highlights.text: Update right from the app. No need to run the installer again.

highlights.title: See what's new first
highlights.text: Every update shows its three best features before you install it.

changes: Update check on start, with an update sheet showing the release's three highlights
Update now downloads the new version over the running script after checking it is newer and really Go2FGym
Later, or tapping outside the sheet, snoozes the offer for two days
Version shown at the bottom of the Train screen
checkUpdates setting to turn update checks off
releases.json, CHANGELOG.md and docs/RELEASING.md for release notes

releases.title: Your next workout in one tap

highlights.title: Instant next workout
highlights.text: Build next creates a plan straight from your history, no form to fill in.

highlights.title: Last workout at a glance
highlights.text: A small chip at the top shows when you last trained, which muscles and how long.

highlights.title: Buttons where you need them
highlights.text: Build workout and Build next now sit in the header of their screens.

changes: Build next in History and Progress builds the plan immediately from the coach's suggestion or your most-due muscle groups, your usual workout length and all your equipment
Loading screen while the next workout is built; Settings opens the pre-filled form
Last-workout chip in the top bar, tap it to open that day in History
Build workout button moved to the builder's header
Export CSV moved to the bottom of History
fixes: A stray white dot showed at the top of the screen
The last-workout chip sat under the camera on iPhones with a Dynamic Island

releases.title: See your progress

highlights.title: Training calendar
highlights.text: See every workout on a month calendar, with dots for the muscle groups trained.

highlights.title: Progress charts
highlights.text: Weekly sets by muscle group, muscle balance, your streak and a trend for each lift.

highlights.title: Strava posts
highlights.text: Get a ready-made Strava title and description in a serious, funny or neutral tone.

changes: History opens on a month calendar with monthly totals per muscle group; List view still available
New Progress tab: 12 weeks of sets stacked by muscle group, 4-week muscle balance with the most-due group, weekly streak, lift trends
Strava title and description per workout in Serious, Funny or Neutral tone, written automatically after each workout; copy title, description or both
Neutral Strava post works without an AI key
fixes: The AI review of a workout could be overwritten when the Strava post was saved right after it

releases.title: Meet your AI coach

highlights.title: AI-built workouts
highlights.text: Pick muscles, equipment, time and intensity, and get a plan with weights from your history.

highlights.title: Post-workout review
highlights.text: After each workout, see what went well, what to focus on next and how hard.

highlights.title: Your own OpenAI key
highlights.text: Uses your OpenAI key, kept in the iPhone Keychain. Everything else works without it.

changes: AI workout builder using only exercises from your library, with sets, reps, rest, weights and form cues
Plan preview with warm-up and cool-down; Start this workout pre-fills every set and uses each exercise's rest time
Automatic AI review after Finish workout, saved with the workout in History
Disclaimer updated to cover AI suggestions and asked again once
One-line installer, like Reading Stars

releases.title: Safer training, more equipment

highlights.title: Resistance bands
highlights.text: 20 band exercises join the library, from pull-aparts to banded squats.

highlights.title: Train-safe reminders
highlights.text: A short own-risk notice to accept once, and a safety tip on every exercise.

highlights.title: Missing-photo hint
highlights.text: The app tells you when some exercises still need their photos downloaded.

changes: Resistance bands added to the default equipment
Own-risk disclaimer to accept on first launch, always available from the Train screen
Safety note under each exercise's steps
Hint on the Train screen when exercises are missing photos

releases.title: Your home gym coach

highlights.title: Pick by muscle
highlights.text: Tap the plates for the muscles you want and get exercises you can do at home.

highlights.title: See it done
highlights.text: Start-to-end photo demos and step-by-step instructions for 446 exercises.

highlights.title: Log every set
highlights.text: Weights and reps prefilled from last time, with a rest timer after each set.

changes: Offline exercise library from free-exercise-db for bodyweight, dumbbell and barbell
Workout logging with rest timer, history, CSV export and iCloud backup
Home Screen widget with your last workout and weekly count
Compact header with a credit to the 7AM Club community
